title: The Nunnehi
summary: The fae of the native peoples of North America.

claims.text: The Nunnehi are faerie spirits born of the myths, dreams and vision quests of the native peoples of North America; the name means people who live anywhere, and they dwell in remote wilds and at the edges of human settlement, guarding against outsiders, European changelings included.

Where European fae hid through a changing ritual, the Nunnehi found willing hosts of deep spirit; the faerie spirit waited within a host until the host had a child, then joined with the child before birth. Many hosts became counselors and healers.
Nunnehi usually return among the descendants of their first hosts, which keeps them tied to their tribes but leaves those whose tribes have died out in grave trouble.
Unlike other changelings, the Nunnehi have lost all touch with their Dreaming homeland, the Higher Hunting Grounds, which some think was destroyed.

title: Rank among the sidhe
summary: How standing really works among the sidhe.

claims.text: The sidhe keep the strictest hierarchy of any kith, showing deference upward and courtesy downward, at least in theory, and present a united front to commoners.
True standing follows intrigue more than title: a noble may keep a title after a dreadful scandal, but the invitations stop arriving and respect can take years to return.

title: The tunghat
summary: Small green Nunnehi bonded to animals.

claims.text: Tunghat are small green folk with darker green hair, nails and teeth, who dress in green and hide under woven grass ponchos; their young can take on the look of their bonded animal.
Their warriors were once the most active; now many have lost heart, and some leave for circus animal acts or veterinary work.
